content.title: About
content.content: Non‑dairy frozen dessert (2218) is a frozen treat made from plant‑based ingredients such as coconut milk, almond milk, or soy cream. It contains no dairy, making it suitable for vegans and people with lactose intolerance, while offering a creamy texture and a wide range of flavors.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first vegan ice cream appeared in the United States in the 1970s.
Emulsifiers like guar gum or carrageenan are often used to achieve a “milky” mouthfeel.
Natural flavorings (berries, fruits, spices) allow for more than 30 distinct taste profiles.
Some brands use fermented nut pastes, giving the dessert a subtle tang.
Non‑dairy ice cream typically has lower saturated fat but can be rich in healthy fats from nuts and coconut.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Plant bases often contain probiotics and prebiotics that promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: The absence of milk sugar makes the product safe for those with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Coconut milk and nut pastes provide medium‑chain triglycerides and monounsaturated fats beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Depending on the base, the dessert can supply vitamin E, magnesium, calcium, and iron.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Natural flavorings such as berries or cocoa contain polyphenols that combat free radicals.

items.title: Nut and soy allergies
items.content: Many plant bases are derived from nuts or soy, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: To enhance taste, added sugars or syrups are common; people monitoring blood glucose should choose unsweetened versions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Even without dairy fats, the dessert can be calorie‑dense due to plant oils.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Emulsifiers and stabilizers (carrageenan, guar gum) are generally safe, but some consumers prefer minimally processed products.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve non‑dairy frozen dessert like any ice cream: in cones, cups, as ice‑cream sandwiches, or blended into smoothies. Pair with berries, nuts, toasted coconut, or a dark‑chocolate sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After opening, consume within 1–2 weeks to prevent ice crystal formation. Avoid thawing and refreezing to maintain texture.
